stories.title: Scheffler Wins Tour Championship — Passes Tiger in Career Earnings, Claims Second FedEx Cup
stories.angle: Scheffler rallied from 3 back on Sunday at East Lake to win Tour Championship and claim 2nd FedExCup; passing Tiger Woods in all-time PGA Tour career earnings ($130M+); joins Tiger and McIlroy as only players with multiple FedEx Cup titles

x_posts.label: Post 1-1
x_posts.text:
Scottie Scheffler rallied from 3 back on Sunday to win the Tour Championship.

$10M. His 2nd FedEx Cup. His 22nd PGA Tour win.

And now? He has PASSED Tiger Woods in all-time PGA Tour career earnings. $130M+.

At 30 years old. The era belongs to Scheffler. #PGATour #FedExCup

x_posts.label: Post 1-2
x_posts.text:
Only 3 players have ever won multiple FedEx Cup titles.

Tiger Woods. Rory McIlroy. And now Scottie Scheffler.

He did it by coming from 3 back on Sunday at East Lake — shooting a final-round 66 to beat Hovland by 3.

This is the top of the game. #PGATour #Scheffler

facebook.long_form:
On Sunday at East Lake, Scottie Scheffler did what Scottie Scheffler does.

He came from behind. He shot 4-under 66 on the final day — tied for the best round of the round — to erase a three-stroke deficit and claim the 2026 Tour Championship. His final score of -16. Viktor Hovland, who led by three entering Sunday, shot 2-over 72 and could only watch as Scheffler walked away with the trophy, the $10 million winner's check, and the FedEx Cup title.

It is Scheffler's second FedEx Cup championship (joining his 2024 title) and his 22nd PGA Tour victory overall. It puts him in the most exclusive club in the history of the FedEx Cup: the only three players to ever win multiple titles are Tiger Woods, Rory McIlroy, and now Scottie Scheffler.

And then there is the number that tells the full story of who Scheffler is as a player: $130 million in career PGA Tour earnings. He has officially surpassed Tiger Woods's all-time record of $120.9 million in official prize money — at 30 years old, with what figures to be the prime of his career still ahead.

Five consecutive No. 1 FedEx Cup seeds. Two FedEx Cup titles. 22 wins. A Masters title. And now, the greatest career earnings number in PGA Tour history.

The era belongs to Scottie Scheffler.
facebook.image_caption: 🏆 Scheffler wins the Tour Championship from 3 back. $10M. Second FedEx Cup. 22 PGA Tour wins. And now: the all-time PGA Tour career earnings record, passing Tiger Woods at $130M+. At age 30. #PGATour #Scheffler #FedExCup

stories.angle: PGA Tour's Captain's Picks show today (Aug 31/Sept 1); final 12-man rosters revealed; Presidents Cup Sept 24-27 at Medinah CC, Illinois; Scheffler leads USA after Tour Championship win

x_posts.text:

After Ryder Cup heartbreak, the Americans are motivated. Presidents Cup can't come fast enough.

#PresidentsCup #Golf

facebook.long_form:
The 2026 Presidents Cup is 23 days away — and today, the final rosters take shape.

The PGA Tour is revealing the captain's picks for both Team USA and the International Team today, completing the 12-man rosters that will compete September 24-27 at Medinah Country Club in Medinah, Illinois.

Captain Brandt Snedeker leads Team USA, which already includes some of the biggest names in the game: Scottie Scheffler (who just won the Tour Championship), Cameron Young, Wyndham Clark, Sam Burns, Russell Henley, and Collin Morikawa. The captain's picks — announced today — fill out the remaining six spots.

Geoff Ogilvy captains the International Team, which draws from players outside the United States and Europe (the Ryder Cup covers Europe). The International side always features strong representation from Australia, South Africa, South Korea, and beyond.

For Team USA, this Presidents Cup carries extra motivation. The 2025 Ryder Cup did not go the way the Americans hoped, and Medinah — one of the most storied venues in American golf — is where they intend to make a statement. Medinah Country Club's Course No. 3 is a par-72 layout stretching 7,657 yards, redesigned in 2024, and it hosts 30 total matches over the four-day competition.

This is team golf's biggest event outside the Ryder Cup. And Team USA is ready to prove it.
facebook.image_caption: 🇺🇸 Presidents Cup captain's picks are in. Team USA — led by Scottie Scheffler — heads to Medinah CC on September 24. After 2025 Ryder Cup heartbreak, the Americans are motivated. #PresidentsCup #PGATour

stories.title: LIV Golf 2.0 — BC Partners Deal Getting Close, Players to Hold Majority Equity
stories.angle: LIV CEO Scott O'Neil: deal signed and approved by board; closing "in September"; BC Partners credit division leading; 10-event schedule (down from 14); players become majority equity holders; PIF exits after 2026

x_posts.label: Post 3
x_posts.text:
LIV Golf CEO Scott O'Neil: "The deal is signed. We expect to close in September."

BC Partners credit division. 10 events. Players as majority equity holders. PIF out.

LIV 2.0 is taking shape — if the A-listers stick around. #LIVGolf #Golf

facebook.long_form:
LIV Golf's survival past 2026 is coming into focus — and the picture looks significantly different from the circuit that launched in 2022.

LIV CEO Scott O'Neil has confirmed that a deal with a new lead investor is signed and approved by the board, with closing expected in September. BC Partners' credit division has been identified as leading financing package discussions, with a deal in the range of $250 million. The arrangement would allow LIV to continue beyond 2026 when the Saudi Public Investment Fund — which has invested $5 billion or more in the league's first four years — officially exits its role as primary backer.

But the LIV Golf that emerges will be a smaller, leaner operation. Here is what LIV 2.0 looks like:

→ 10 annual events (down from 14 in 2026)
→ 5 events in the United States, 5 internationally
→ Significantly reduced tournament purses
→ Players become majority equity holders — a model O'Neil called "a first for a major global sports league"

The critical condition: enough of LIV's marquee names must commit to 2027 for investors to feel confident. Commissioner Greg Norman has said he cannot guarantee the 2027 season. Poulter has expressed uncertainty. Dozens of players remain under contract — but their willingness to accept equity over cash is the open question.

LIV's 2026 season concluded with Jon Rahm claiming his third consecutive individual title and La Sasso winning the Indianapolis finale. The league's competitive product has been compelling. Whether the financial model can be reborn under new ownership is the story of the next 30 days.
facebook.image_caption: ⛳ LIV Golf's new deal is signed — closing "in September." BC Partners. 10 events. Players as equity holders. PIF exits after 2026. LIV 2.0 is almost here — if the stars stay. #LIVGolf #Golf

stories.title: PGA Tour Fall Schedule Preview — Biltmore Championship Next, Presidents Cup, Bank of Utah
stories.angle: Tour Championship concluded; fall schedule kicks off; 3 events in September-October; good timing to preview what's next for the world's top players

x_posts.label: Post 4
x_posts.text:
The Tour Championship is over.

What's next on the PGA Tour:
🏌️ Biltmore Championship — Sept 17-20, Asheville NC
🤝 Presidents Cup — Sept 24-27, Medinah IL
🏌️ Bank of Utah Championship — Oct 1-4, Ivins UT

The fall season is here. #PGATour #Golf

facebook.long_form:
The Tour Championship is done. Scottie Scheffler has his FedEx Cup trophy. And now, the PGA Tour calendar pivots to its fall chapter.

Here is what is coming up over the next six weeks for professional golf's most watched circuit:

🏌️ **Biltmore Championship — September 17-20**
Location: The Cliffs at Walnut Cove, Asheville, North Carolina. A scenic fall destination event that gives players a chance to shake off the end-of-summer grind before team competition arrives.

🤝 **Presidents Cup — September 24-27**
Location: Medinah Country Club, Medinah, Illinois. Team USA (captained by Brandt Snedeker) vs. the International Team (captained by Geoff Ogilvy). This is the marquee event of the fall schedule — and with Scottie Scheffler anchoring the American side, Team USA has a formidable lineup.

🏌️ **Bank of Utah Championship — October 1-4**
Location: Ivins, Utah. A fall event that gives players at the fringes of the Tour a chance to build momentum heading into the off-season.

For the sport's elite, the coming weeks bring a mix of team pride and individual preparation. After the intensity of the FedEx Cup Playoffs, the fall schedule offers a different kind of pressure — and a different kind of reward.
facebook.image_caption: ⛳ The Tour Championship is over. Here is what is next on the PGA Tour: Biltmore Championship (Sept 17-20), Presidents Cup (Sept 24-27 at Medinah), Bank of Utah Championship (Oct 1-4). Fall golf is here. #PGATour #Golf

stories.title: Solheim Cup 2026 — USA vs. Europe in the Netherlands, 10 Days Away
stories.angle: Solheim Cup is Sept 11-13 in 's-Hertogenbosch (Den Bosch), Netherlands; USA LPGA stars looking to deliver after Ryder Cup year; 10 days to tee time

x_posts.label: Post 5
x_posts.text:
The Solheim Cup is 10 days away.

Team USA vs. Team Europe. September 11-13 in 's-Hertogenbosch, Netherlands.

The best women golfers in the world competing for pride, country, and the Solheim. It's going to be 🔥

#SolheimCup #LPGA #Golf

facebook.long_form:
In 10 days, the best women golfers in the world will face off at one of the sport's most prestigious team competitions — and it is happening in the Netherlands.

The 2026 Solheim Cup takes place September 11-13 at 's-Hertogenbosch (Den Bosch), in the Netherlands. Team USA faces Team Europe in the biennial match-play competition that mirrors the Ryder Cup in its intensity and its stakes. Twenty-eight players — 14 per side, drawn from the LPGA Tour and the Ladies European Tour — compete for the Solheim Cup trophy and the pride of their respective federations.

The 2026 LPGA Tour season has been impressive, with players like Ruoning Yin — who just won the FM Championship at TPC Boston on August 30 — showcasing the depth of talent on the American side. Meanwhile, European players on the LET have been competitive all season, making this a genuinely unpredictable match-play showdown.

After the emotional intensity of any Ryder Cup year, the Solheim Cup carries its own charge. Women's golf's biggest team event deserves the spotlight it gets every two years. The Netherlands in September is a spectacular backdrop.

Ten days. Count them down.
facebook.image_caption: 🏌️ Solheim Cup 2026 starts in 10 days. Team USA vs. Team Europe in the Netherlands — September 11-13. Women's golf's biggest team event. #SolheimCup #LPGA #Golf
